pages.note: S1. Fetched OK (also .md variant). Page is silent on development workspace and on testing.
S2. Fetched OK. Says where the Authorization URL is, not when it is populated.
Extra page, read for redirect_uri rules. No format rules.

claims.claim: Authorization URL field populates only after the connection is submitted for review
claims.quote: The Authorization URL field populates after a public connection is submitted for review
claims.correction: Quote is an image caption under the Configuration tab screenshot, not body text. The fact (field is empty until submission) is as the docs state. No official page says whether the URL is usable in the development workspace, or what 'review' means (Marketplace review vs connection review), or its timeline. Public-connections page says only: 'Find this URL in the Configuration tab of your connection in the Developer portal.' Keep the claim at 'field populates after submission' and do not imply the URL is unusable in the dev workspace.

claims.claim: You cannot hand out the authorization URL until submitted for review
claims.quote: The Authorization URL field populates after a public connection is submitted for review
claims.correction: Overstated. Docs only say the Configuration-tab field is populated after submission. They do not say the flow cannot be run or tested earlier, nor that it is 'locked'. Reword: 'The Authorization URL field in the portal is empty until you submit the connection for review; docs do not say whether the flow works earlier (e.g. in the dev workspace).'

claims.claim: Developer portal access with a development workspace
claims.quote: Connection name and development workspace
claims.correction: Quote is from the required-fields list (paraphrase of list item). Dev workspace is a required creation field.

claims.claim: One or more redirect URIs
claims.quote: Redirect URI(s) for the OAuth flow

claims.claim: Installation scope Any workspace vs Selected workspaces; cannot be changed; only Any workspace is Marketplace-eligible
claims.quote: Installation scope is set once, at creation time, and can't be changed afterward.
claims.correction: Marketplace: 'Only public connections with an installation scope of Any workspace can be listed on the Marketplace.' (marketplace-listing page). Also: if you picked Selected workspaces and later want to list, create a new connection.

claims.claim: Developer portal, Build sidebar, Public connections, Create new connection
claims.quote: In the Build section of the sidebar, select Public connections.

claims.claim: Form fields: name, dev workspace, redirect URIs, installation scope, capabilities
claims.quote: Click Create new connection and fill in the required fields
claims.correction: Field list (name, development workspace, redirect URIs, installation scope, capabilities) is from the page's list under that sentence; paraphrase only for the list.

claims.claim: Client ID and secret on Configuration tab
claims.quote: After creation, visit the Configuration tab to retrieve your OAuth client ID and OAuth client secret.

claims.claim: Auth URL params client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, owner=user, state optional
claims.quote: Always use user.
claims.correction: owner: 'Always use user.' state: 'It can also be used to prevent CSRF attacks.' Required params per page summary: client_id, redirect_uri, response_type, owner; state optional (paraphrase only for the required list). The 'populates after review' note: see first claim.

claims.claim: POST code to https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token with HTTP Basic auth CLIENT_ID:CLIENT_SECRET
claims.quote: The request is authorized using HTTP Basic Authentication.
claims.correction: Endpoint URL https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token stated on same page; credentials are base64-encoded CLIENT_ID:CLIENT_SECRET.

claims.claim: Store access and refresh tokens; refresh returns new access and new refresh token
claims.quote: Refreshing an access token will generate a new access token and a new refresh token.

claims.claim: Marketplace: save draft, Listings > Connections, submit for review, email feedback, resubmit
claims.quote: If changes are required, the Notion team sends feedback and you can resubmit after making updates.
claims.correction: Also: 'Save your listing as a draft.' and 'From the Listings > Connections page, find your draft listing.'

claims.claim: redirect_uri in token request required if passed as query param in auth URL or if more than one redirect URI configured
claims.quote: If there are more than one redirect URIs included in your connection settings, this field is required.
claims.correction: Also 'If the redirect URI was supplied as a query param in the Authorization URL, this field is required.' Note the Create a token reference additionally says the field 'is not allowed in the request body if there is one redirect_uri included in the connection's settings' (see missing).

claims.claim: No redirect URI format rules (HTTPS, localhost) stated
claims.correction: Still not stated on S1, S2 or the Create a token reference (redirect_uri is a plain string). Authorization page only links to https://www.oauth.com/oauth2-servers/redirect-uris/ for general background. Remains unverified; the guide's U() framing is correct.

claims.claim: Capabilities: Read/Update/Insert content; Read/Insert comments; user info none / without email / with email
claims.quote: No user information, User information without email addresses, User information with email addresses
claims.correction: Content: 'Read content', 'Update content', 'Insert content'. Comments: 'Read comments', 'Insert comments'. Names match.

claims.claim: Capability change forces re-authentication; request only what you need
claims.quote: users will need to re-authenticate with a connection if the capabilities are changed.
claims.correction: Also: 'you want to request minimum capabilities that your connection needs in order to function.'

claims.claim: No testing mode described; each user authorizes individually; unconfirmed whether dev workspace can use connection before review
claims.quote: each prospective user needs to individually follow the auth flow for the connection.
claims.correction: The individual-authorization sentence is confirmed. No official page read mentions testing or dev-workspace use before review (S1, S2 explicitly silent), so testing-before-review cannot be confirmed. Remains U().

claims.claim: Marketplace only for Any workspace; 5-10 business days by email; rejections from brand/trademark to quality
claims.quote: After submission, expect to hear back from our team within 5-10 business days via email.
claims.correction: 'Connections are rejected for various reasons, from brand/trademark issues to quality concerns.'

claims.claim: 5-10 business days for Marketplace listing; unclear if it covers the connection review
claims.quote: After submission, expect to hear back from our team within 5-10 business days via email.
claims.correction: The sentence is on the Marketplace listing page and follows submission of the listing; the guide's scope (Marketplace listing) is correct. Nothing official ties it to the connection review that populates the Authorization URL, so the guide's hedge is right and that link stays unsupported. 'status: documented' is OK for listing only.

claims.claim: Installation scope permanent; create new connection if wrong
claims.quote: Installation scope is set once, at creation time, and can't be changed afterward.
claims.correction: Authorization page also: 'This can't be changed after creation.'

claims.claim: Selected-workspace connections not Marketplace-eligible
claims.quote: Only public connections with an installation scope of Any workspace can be listed on the Marketplace.

claims.claim: Capability changes force re-consent for every user
claims.quote: users will need to re-authenticate with a connection if the capabilities are changed.
claims.correction: 'Every user' is a mild generalisation of 'users'.

claims.claim: Each user authorizes individually; no shared workspace-wide grant
claims.quote: each prospective user needs to individually follow the auth flow for the connection.
claims.correction: First half confirmed. 'There is no shared workspace-wide grant' is the guide's inference and not stated; drop it or label it as inference. Related stated fact: 'After a user authorizes a public connection, only that user can interact with the connection in their workspace.' (public-connections page).

claims.claim: Setup is a form in the portal; no timeline/criteria for the review step; scope fixed at creation
claims.quote: The Authorization URL field populates after a public connection is submitted for review
claims.correction: No timeline or criteria for connection review found on S1 or S2 (absence only; 5-10 days is for Marketplace listing). Soften 'no timeline' to 'none found on the pages read'.

claims.claim: ~1-3 h hands-on
claims.correction: Self-labelled estimate; no official source.

claims.claim: Unknown whether connection is usable in dev workspace before review
claims.correction: Still not stated on any official page read. Keep as unknown.

missing: Create a token reference says redirect_uri 'is not allowed in the request body if there is one redirect_uri included in the connection's settings' and 'In most cases, the redirect_uri field is required.' This sits oddly beside 'required if set as query param' and is a likely source of invalid_request/redirect errors; worth stating precisely. https://developers.notion.com/reference/create-a-token

Authorization page: set the Notion-Version and Content-type headers in all requests ('the Notion-Version and Content-type headers in all of your requests'), and store the whole token pair/response, since Notion may return a new access_token and refresh_token on re-authorization. https://developers.notion.com/guides/get-started/authorization

Authorization page: partial authorization and page picker caveats. If the user does not complete the flow, the connection will not have access to the selected pages; the picker only shows pages/databases the user has full access to. https://developers.notion.com/guides/get-started/authorization
